primitives.verbatim_quote: **Compact logit transform (Algorithm 2)** for overconfident models: pre-transform scores with G_ε (scaled/shifted logit on [ε,1-ε], identity outside), then run Algorithm 1; ε = 10^(r-1) with r = ⌊log10(min(1-p_i))⌋.
primitives.assumptions: Model outputs are bounded away from 0 and 1; overconfidence is present in extreme tail probabilities.

The core idea of spline-based calibration is to replace rigid parametric methods like Platt scaling or isotonic regression with a flexible, smooth approximation. It begins with a set of model scores and their corresponding true outcomes, forming a calibration dataset. A non-parametric logistic regression is then applied, where the score space is expanded into a natural cubic spline basis. The resulting function f(z) maps input scores z to calibrated probabilities. Cross-validation selects optimal regularization strength λ to prevent overfitting. For overconfident models, the compact logit transform adjusts extreme probabilities before calibration. In multi-class settings, each class is handled independently using one-vs-rest encoding, followed by renormalization. This approach ensures that even complex, high-dimensional models can be post-processed into reliable probabilistic forecasts without requiring retraining.
